```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, comment = "")
options(width = 160)
```

This file simulates the four studies proposed in the design memo of Studies 2 to 5 (`Docs/Memorandum/`) and reports how often each planned test would detect the effect it is meant to detect. The memo of November 17, 2026 called them Experiments 3A to 3D of a Study 3; since November 18 they are Study 2 (with a mouse-tracked condition added), Study 3, Study 4 and Study 5. Every simulated data set has the structure of the planned design (participants crossed with items, two genres per participant where the design calls for it), and every test is the mixed-effects model the memo proposes, with a Wald test at the .05 level.

**Where the numbers come from.** For the rating tasks, the standard deviations of the participant, item and residual terms are those of Study 1's registered ratings model, read from `v4_rebuild/18_studies2to5_design/study1_h2_variance_components.csv` (written by `design_inputs_from_study1.Rmd`). Effect sizes are stated in each section. Where Study 1 gives no estimate (the curvature of mouse paths in Study 2 and the comparison of two works in Study 4), the assumed values are stated and are assumptions, not data.

**How to run.** Knit with parameters: `sims` is the number of simulated data sets per scenario (200 gives a standard error of about .03 at a power of .80) and `workers` the number of processes.

```{r packages}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(lme4); library(ggplot2); library(knitr) })
SIMS <- as.integer(params$sims); WORKERS <- max(1L, min(as.integer(params$workers), parallel::detectCores() - 2L)); SEED <- 20260219
input <- tryCatch(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE), error = function(e) NULL)
HERE <- if (!is.null(input)) dirname(normalizePath(input)) else normalizePath(getwd())
OUT <- normalizePath(file.path(HERE, "..", "v4_rebuild", "18_studies2to5_design"))
dir.create(file.path(OUT, "figures"), showWarnings = FALSE)
vc <- read.csv(file.path(OUT, "study1_h2_variance_components.csv"))
sdv <- function(g, t = NA) vc$sd[vc$group == g & (if (is.na(t)) is.na(vc$term) else vc$term %in% t)]
S1 <- list(item = sdv("item", "(Intercept)"), pid = vc$sd[grepl("^pid", vc$group) & vc$term == "(Intercept)"],
           slopeD = vc$sd[grepl("^pid", vc$group) & vc$term == "D"], slopeP = vc$sd[grepl("^pid", vc$group) & vc$term == "P"], resid = sdv("Residual"))
str(S1)
CTRL <- lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", calc.derivs = FALSE)
wald <- function(m, L) {                         # estimate, standard error and z for a contrast of the fixed effects
  b <- fixef(m); V <- as.matrix(vcov(m)); l <- setNames(numeric(length(b)), names(b)); l[names(L)] <- L
  est <- sum(l * b); se <- sqrt(as.numeric(t(l) %*% V %*% l)); c(est = est, se = se, z = est / se)
}
run_grid <- function(grid, one, export) {        # one(row, s) returns a named numeric vector for simulation s
  cl <- parallel::makePSOCKcluster(WORKERS); on.exit(parallel::stopCluster(cl))
  parallel::clusterEvalQ(cl, suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(lme4)))
  parallel::clusterExport(cl, c(export, "wald", "CTRL", "S1", "SEED", "PAIRS"), envir = globalenv())
  jobs <- expand.grid(row = seq_len(nrow(grid)), s = seq_len(SIMS))
  environment(one) <- globalenv()                  # send the function itself; on a worker it finds its helpers in the global environment
  res <- parallel::parLapplyLB(cl, seq_len(nrow(jobs)), function(k, jobs, grid, one, seed) {
    set.seed(seed + 1000 * jobs$row[k] + jobs$s[k])
    c(row = jobs$row[k], tryCatch(one(grid[jobs$row[k], ], jobs$s[k]), error = function(e) NULL))
  }, jobs = jobs, grid = grid, one = one, seed = SEED)
  res <- do.call(rbind, res[vapply(res, length, 0L) > 1])
  agg <- aggregate(res[, -1, drop = FALSE], list(row = res[, "row"]), mean)
  cbind(grid[agg$row, , drop = FALSE], agg[, -1, drop = FALSE])
}
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 13))
PAIRS <- rbind(c(1, 2), c(3, 4), c(5, 6), c(1, 3), c(2, 5), c(4, 6))         # the six genre pairs of the Study 1 schedule
```

# Study 2: one shared feature, three rated questions

**Design simulated.** Each participant answers one question (the question varies between participants) about the Study 1 items of two genres. Items are crossed with participants within a genre. Prevalence (P) and distinctiveness (D) are coded +0.5 for a genre's top third and −0.5 for its bottom third, as in Study 1. The item set is either the 288 items Study 1 rated (12 per cell per genre) or an extended set of 432 (18 per cell per genre).

**The copying question under three accounts.** The scenarios give the effect of P and of D, in rating points, on judged evidence of copying:

- *query-sensitive*: P −0.60, D 0 (prevalence lowers the evidence; distinctiveness is irrelevant);
- *one intuition*: P −0.25, D −1.04 (seven tenths of Study 1's expectedness effects, reversed in sign);
- *overall frequency*: P −0.60, D +0.60 (features that are rare in film generally count for more).

**Tests.** (1) the contrast P minus D, the analogue of Study 1's H2c, whose sign separates the first account (negative) from the second (positive); (2) the effect of D alone; (3) equivalence of the D effect to zero within ±0.40 and within ±0.30 rating points (two one-sided tests, so the 90% interval must lie inside the bounds); (4) the effect of P alone.

```{r sim-study2-ratings}
make_s2 <- function(n, per_cell, bP, bD) {
  items <- expand.grid(k = seq_len(per_cell), P = c(-.5, .5), D = c(-.5, .5), genre = 1:6)
  items$item <- seq_len(nrow(items)); items$w <- rnorm(nrow(items), 0, S1$item)
  pid <- seq_len(n); pair <- PAIRS[(pid - 1) %% 6 + 1, , drop = FALSE]
  u0 <- rnorm(n, 0, S1$pid); uD <- rnorm(n, 0, S1$slopeD); uP <- rnorm(n, 0, S1$slopeP)
  d <- do.call(rbind, lapply(pid, function(i) { x <- items[items$genre %in% pair[i, ], ]; x$pid <- i; x }))
  d$y <- 4 + (bP + uP[d$pid]) * d$P + (bD + uD[d$pid]) * d$D + u0[d$pid] + d$w + rnorm(nrow(d), 0, S1$resid)
  d$genre <- factor(d$genre); d
}
one_s2 <- function(g, s) {
  d <- make_s2(g$n, g$per_cell, g$bP, g$bD)
  m <- lmer(y ~ P + D + P:D + genre + (1 | pid) + (0 + D | pid) + (1 | item), d, control = CTRL)
  c1 <- wald(m, c(P = 1, D = -1)); cD <- wald(m, c(D = 1)); cP <- wald(m, c(P = 1))
  tost <- function(b) as.numeric(cD["est"] - 1.645 * cD["se"] > -b && cD["est"] + 1.645 * cD["se"] < b)
  c(P_minus_D_sig = as.numeric(abs(c1["z"]) > 1.96), P_minus_D_negative = as.numeric(c1["z"] < -1.96), P_minus_D_positive = as.numeric(c1["z"] > 1.96),
    D_sig = as.numeric(abs(cD["z"]) > 1.96), D_equiv_040 = tost(0.40), D_equiv_030 = tost(0.30), P_sig = as.numeric(abs(cP["z"]) > 1.96),
    se_D = as.numeric(cD["se"]), se_P = as.numeric(cP["se"]), se_P_minus_D = as.numeric(c1["se"]))
}
sc <- data.frame(account = c("query-sensitive", "one intuition", "overall frequency"), bP = c(-.60, -.25, -.60), bD = c(0, -1.04, .60))
grid_s2 <- merge(merge(sc, data.frame(n = c(50, 70, 90))), data.frame(per_cell = c(12, 18)))
res_s2 <- run_grid(grid_s2, one_s2, "make_s2")
res_s2$items <- res_s2$per_cell * 24
write.csv(res_s2, file.path(OUT, "power_study2_ratings.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
kable(res_s2[order(res_s2$account, res_s2$items, res_s2$n), c("account", "items", "n", "P_minus_D_negative", "P_minus_D_positive", "D_sig", "D_equiv_040", "D_equiv_030", "P_sig", "se_D", "se_P_minus_D")],
      digits = 2, row.names = FALSE, caption = "Study 2, copying rating: share of simulations in which each test gives the stated result (n = participants in that condition)")
```

```{r fig-study2-ratings, fig.width = 9.1, fig.height = 4}
f <- res_s2[res_s2$account == "query-sensitive", ]
long <- rbind(data.frame(n = f$n, items = f$items, test = "D equivalent to zero within ±0.40", power = f$D_equiv_040),
              data.frame(n = f$n, items = f$items, test = "D equivalent to zero within ±0.30", power = f$D_equiv_030),
              data.frame(n = f$n, items = f$items, test = "P minus D below zero", power = f$P_minus_D_negative))
long$items <- factor(paste(long$items, "items"))
p <- ggplot(long, aes(n, power, colour = test, shape = test)) + geom_line() + geom_point(size = 3) + facet_wrap(~ items) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = .8, linetype = "dashed") + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, .2)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(50, 70, 90)) + scale_colour_manual(values = c("#7f7f7f", "#d62728", "#1f77b4"), name = NULL) + scale_shape_discrete(name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Participants rating the copying question", y = "Share of simulations (power)",
       title = "Study 2 ratings, if copying judgments follow prevalence only") + theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")
print(p); ggsave(file.path(OUT, "figures", "power_study2_ratings.png"), p, width = 9.1, height = 5, dpi = 200, bg = "white")
```

# Study 2: the mouse-tracked copying choice

**Design simulated.** Participants in the tracked condition make the copying judgment as a choice between two boxes, "Copied" and "Coincidence", for the same items and the same two genres as the rating conditions. Two things are analysed: the choice itself, and how far the mouse path bends toward the box that was not chosen.

## The choice

**From ratings to choices.** A choice is treated as the copying rating cut at the participant's own threshold, with the same trial-to-trial noise. Under that assumption a rating effect of $b$ points is a probit effect of $b$ divided by the residual standard deviation, and a logit effect about 1.7 times that. Every Study 1 standard deviation is converted the same way. This is an assumption: a speeded choice may be noisier than a rating, which would lower the power below the figures here.

**Scenarios and tests.** The three accounts are those of the rating simulation, converted to logits. The tests are the same four: the contrast P minus D, the effect of D, equivalence of the D effect to zero within the logit equivalent of ±0.40 rating points, and the effect of P. A last scenario sets the overall rate of "Copied" at about a quarter instead of a half. The model is a logistic mixed model with the same terms as the rating model. To keep the simulation fast it is fit with `nAGQ = 0`, which is slightly conservative for the fixed effects; the registered analysis would use the Laplace approximation.

```{r sim-study2-choice}
K <- 1.7 / S1$resid                                   # rating points to logits
LG <- list(item = K * S1$item, pid = K * S1$pid, slopeD = K * S1$slopeD, slopeP = K * S1$slopeP)
EQ_LOGIT <- K * 0.40
GCTRL <- glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", calc.derivs = FALSE)
make_s2c <- function(n, per_cell, bP, bD, b0, k_genres = 2) {   # bP, bD in logits; b0 is the logit of the overall rate of "Copied"
  items <- expand.grid(k = seq_len(per_cell), P = c(-.5, .5), D = c(-.5, .5), genre = 1:6)
  items$item <- seq_len(nrow(items)); items$w <- rnorm(nrow(items), 0, LG$item)
  pid <- seq_len(n); pair <- PAIRS[(pid - 1) %% 6 + 1, , drop = FALSE]
  u0 <- rnorm(n, 0, LG$pid); uD <- rnorm(n, 0, LG$slopeD); uP <- rnorm(n, 0, LG$slopeP)
  d <- do.call(rbind, lapply(pid, function(i) { x <- if (k_genres == 2) items[items$genre %in% pair[i, ], ] else items; x$pid <- i; x }))
  eta <- b0 + (bP + uP[d$pid]) * d$P + (bD + uD[d$pid]) * d$D + u0[d$pid] + d$w
  d$copied <- rbinom(nrow(d), 1, plogis(eta)); d$genre <- factor(d$genre); d
}
one_s2c <- function(g, s) {
  d <- make_s2c(g$n, g$per_cell, g$bP, g$bD, g$b0)
  m <- glmer(copied ~ P + D + P:D + genre + (1 | pid) + (0 + D | pid) + (1 | item), d, family = binomial, nAGQ = 0, control = GCTRL)
  c1 <- wald(m, c(P = 1, D = -1)); cD <- wald(m, c(D = 1)); cP <- wald(m, c(P = 1))
  tost <- as.numeric(cD["est"] - 1.645 * cD["se"] > -EQ_LOGIT && cD["est"] + 1.645 * cD["se"] < EQ_LOGIT)
  c(P_minus_D_negative = as.numeric(c1["z"] < -1.96), P_minus_D_positive = as.numeric(c1["z"] > 1.96), D_sig = as.numeric(abs(cD["z"]) > 1.96),
    D_equiv = tost, P_sig = as.numeric(abs(cP["z"]) > 1.96), se_D = as.numeric(cD["se"]), se_P_minus_D = as.numeric(c1["se"]), share_copied = mean(d$copied))
}
sc_c <- data.frame(account = c("query-sensitive", "one intuition", "overall frequency"), bP = K * c(-.60, -.25, -.60), bD = K * c(0, -1.04, .60), b0 = 0)
grid_s2c <- merge(merge(sc_c, data.frame(n = c(50, 70, 90))), data.frame(per_cell = c(12, 18)))
grid_s2c <- rbind(grid_s2c, data.frame(account = "query-sensitive, a quarter Copied", bP = K * -.60, bD = 0, b0 = qlogis(.25), n = 70, per_cell = c(12, 18)))
res_s2c <- run_grid(grid_s2c, one_s2c, c("make_s2c", "LG", "EQ_LOGIT", "GCTRL", "K"))
res_s2c$items <- res_s2c$per_cell * 24
write.csv(res_s2c, file.path(OUT, "power_study2_choice.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
cat("one rating point =", round(K, 2), "logits; equivalence bound = ±", round(EQ_LOGIT, 2), "logits\n")
kable(res_s2c[order(res_s2c$account, res_s2c$items, res_s2c$n), c("account", "items", "n", "share_copied", "P_minus_D_negative", "P_minus_D_positive", "D_sig", "D_equiv", "P_sig", "se_D", "se_P_minus_D")],
      digits = 2, row.names = FALSE, caption = "Study 2, tracked condition, choice of Copied: share of simulations in which each test gives the stated result (n = participants in the tracked condition; standard errors in logits)")
```

## The path of the mouse

**Measure and test.** For each trial the curvature is the area between the mouse path and a straight line from the start to the chosen box, positive when the path bends toward the box that was not chosen. The registered question is whether the path bends more when the response goes against what is typical of the genre: "Copied" chosen for a characteristic feature, or "Coincidence" chosen for an uncharacteristic one. That is the response by distinctiveness interaction (*conflict with distinctiveness*); the response by prevalence interaction (*conflict with prevalence*) is its counterpart. The simulation draws the choices from the query-sensitive account, in which distinctiveness has no effect on what people choose, and then gives the path a pull toward the typical answer. This is the case the tracked condition exists to detect: an intuition that moves the hand and is overruled.

**Assumed values (not from data).** Curvature is in units of its own trial-to-trial standard deviation. Participant SD 0.6; participant slope SD for each conflict term 0.15; item SD 0.15; residual SD 1. The pull from distinctiveness is 0.10, 0.15 or 0.20 of a trial SD and the pull from prevalence 0.10. No estimate exists for this judgment. The Stroop trials at the start of each tracked session give a known conflict effect on the same measure, and the pulls can be scaled against it once data exist.

**More trials.** The last rows give each tracked participant all six genres (288 item trials) instead of two (96), to show what tripling the trials would buy.

```{r sim-study2-curvature}
make_s2t <- function(n, per_cell, pullD, pullP, k_genres) {
  d <- make_s2c(n, per_cell, K * -.60, 0, 0, k_genres)          # choices follow prevalence only
  resp <- d$copied - .5
  d$resp <- resp; d$cD <- 2 * resp * d$D; d$cP <- 2 * resp * d$P        # +.5 when the response goes against what the feature's level suggests
  a <- rnorm(n, 0, 0.6); vD <- rnorm(n, 0, 0.15); vP <- rnorm(n, 0, 0.15); wi <- rnorm(max(d$item), 0, 0.15)
  d$y <- (pullD + vD[d$pid]) * d$cD + (pullP + vP[d$pid]) * d$cP + a[d$pid] + wi[d$item] + rnorm(nrow(d)); d
}
one_s2t <- function(g, s) {
  d <- make_s2t(g$n, g$per_cell, g$pullD, g$pullP, g$k_genres)
  m <- lmer(y ~ resp + P + D + cD + cP + genre + (1 | pid) + (0 + cD | pid) + (1 | item), d, control = CTRL)
  wD <- wald(m, c(cD = 1)); wP <- wald(m, c(cP = 1)); wdiff <- wald(m, c(cD = 1, cP = -1))
  c(pull_D = as.numeric(abs(wD["z"]) > 1.96), pull_P = as.numeric(abs(wP["z"]) > 1.96), D_minus_P = as.numeric(abs(wdiff["z"]) > 1.96),
    se_pull_D = as.numeric(wD["se"]), trials = nrow(d) / g$n)
}
grid_s2t <- expand.grid(n = c(50, 70, 90), per_cell = c(12, 18), pullD = c(0.10, 0.15, 0.20), pullP = 0.10, k_genres = 2)
grid_s2t <- rbind(grid_s2t, expand.grid(n = 70, per_cell = 12, pullD = c(0.10, 0.15, 0.20), pullP = 0.10, k_genres = 6))
res_s2t <- run_grid(grid_s2t, one_s2t, c("make_s2t", "make_s2c", "LG", "K"))
res_s2t$items <- res_s2t$per_cell * 24
write.csv(res_s2t, file.path(OUT, "power_study2_tracking.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
kable(res_s2t[order(res_s2t$k_genres, res_s2t$pullD, res_s2t$items, res_s2t$n), c("k_genres", "pullD", "items", "n", "trials", "pull_D", "pull_P", "D_minus_P", "se_pull_D")],
      digits = 2, row.names = FALSE, caption = "Study 2, tracked condition, curvature: power to detect a pull toward the typical answer (pullD, in trial SDs) when choices follow prevalence only; pull_P is the power for the prevalence pull of 0.10; k_genres = genres per participant; trials = item trials per participant")
```

```{r fig-study2-tracking, fig.width = 9.1, fig.height = 4}
f <- res_s2t[res_s2t$k_genres == 2, ]
f$items <- factor(paste(f$items, "items")); f$size <- factor(sprintf("%.2f", f$pullD))
p <- ggplot(f, aes(n, pull_D, colour = size, shape = size)) + geom_line() + geom_point(size = 3) + facet_wrap(~ items) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = .8, linetype = "dashed") + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, .2)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(50, 70, 90)) + scale_colour_manual(values = c("#7f7f7f", "#1f77b4", "#d62728"), name = "Pull toward the typical answer (trial SDs)") +
  scale_shape_discrete(name = "Pull toward the typical answer (trial SDs)") +
  labs(x = "Participants in the tracked condition", y = "Share of simulations (power)", title = "Study 2 tracked condition: detecting a pull that choices do not show") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
print(p); ggsave(file.path(OUT, "figures", "power_study2_tracking.png"), p, width = 9.1, height = 5, dpi = 200, bg = "white")
```

# Study 3: packages of shared features

**Design simulated.** Each participant rates how strongly a pair of shared features suggests copying, for the pairs of two genres. Half the pairs are *implied* (one feature nearly implies the other in the genre) and half *unrelated*, matched on each member's prevalence. The test is the effect of pair type. Under the model, implied pairs are weaker evidence; if people neglect the dependence there is no effect, and if a coherent package feels like more similarity the effect reverses. Pair and participant standard deviations are Study 1's item and participant values; the participant slope for pair type is assumed equal to Study 1's slope for distinctiveness.

```{r sim-study3}
make_s3 <- function(n, per_type, delta) {
  items <- expand.grid(k = seq_len(per_type), type = c(-.5, .5), genre = 1:6); items$item <- seq_len(nrow(items)); items$w <- rnorm(nrow(items), 0, S1$item)
  pid <- seq_len(n); pair <- PAIRS[(pid - 1) %% 6 + 1, , drop = FALSE]
  u0 <- rnorm(n, 0, S1$pid); u1 <- rnorm(n, 0, S1$slopeD)
  d <- do.call(rbind, lapply(pid, function(i) { x <- items[items$genre %in% pair[i, ], ]; x$pid <- i; x }))
  d$y <- 4 + (delta + u1[d$pid]) * d$type + u0[d$pid] + d$w + rnorm(nrow(d), 0, S1$resid); d$genre <- factor(d$genre); d
}
one_s3 <- function(g, s) {
  d <- make_s3(g$n, g$per_type, g$delta)
  m <- lmer(y ~ type + genre + (1 | pid) + (0 + type | pid) + (1 | item), d, control = CTRL)
  w <- wald(m, c(type = 1)); c(type_sig = as.numeric(abs(w["z"]) > 1.96), se = as.numeric(w["se"]))
}
grid_s3 <- expand.grid(n = c(60, 80, 100), per_type = c(8, 12), delta = c(0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6))
res_s3 <- run_grid(grid_s3, one_s3, "make_s3")
res_s3$pairs <- res_s3$per_type * 12
write.csv(res_s3, file.path(OUT, "power_study3.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
kable(res_s3[order(res_s3$delta, res_s3$pairs, res_s3$n), c("delta", "pairs", "n", "type_sig", "se")], digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
      caption = "Study 3, unmatched pairs: power to detect a difference of delta rating points between implied and unrelated pairs")
```

**Matched sets.** The unmatched design is limited by how much pairs differ from one another. A matched design removes part of that: each implied pair is matched to an unrelated pair that shares its second feature, with first features of equal prevalence (a foreman and a ranch; a traveler and a ranch). The two pairs of a set then share whatever is specific to the common feature. The simulation gives each set its own deviation and each pair a further one. How the pair variance divides between the two is not known; the simulation assumes half is shared within a set (an assumption) and, as a pessimistic case, a quarter.

```{r sim-study3-matched}
make_s3m <- function(n, sets, delta, share) {
  st <- expand.grid(k = seq_len(sets), genre = 1:6); st$set <- seq_len(nrow(st)); st$ws <- rnorm(nrow(st), 0, S1$item * sqrt(share))
  items <- rbind(cbind(st, type = -.5), cbind(st, type = .5)); items$item <- seq_len(nrow(items)); items$w <- items$ws + rnorm(nrow(items), 0, S1$item * sqrt(1 - share))
  pid <- seq_len(n); pair <- PAIRS[(pid - 1) %% 6 + 1, , drop = FALSE]
  u0 <- rnorm(n, 0, S1$pid); u1 <- rnorm(n, 0, S1$slopeD)
  d <- do.call(rbind, lapply(pid, function(i) { x <- items[items$genre %in% pair[i, ], ]; x$pid <- i; x }))
  d$y <- 4 + (delta + u1[d$pid]) * d$type + u0[d$pid] + d$w + rnorm(nrow(d), 0, S1$resid); d$genre <- factor(d$genre); d
}
one_s3m <- function(g, s) {
  d <- make_s3m(g$n, g$sets, g$delta, g$share)
  m <- lmer(y ~ type + genre + (1 | pid) + (0 + type | pid) + (1 | set) + (1 | item), d, control = CTRL)
  w <- wald(m, c(type = 1)); c(type_sig = as.numeric(abs(w["z"]) > 1.96), se = as.numeric(w["se"]))
}
grid_s3m <- expand.grid(n = c(60, 80), sets = c(8, 12), delta = c(0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6), share = c(0.25, 0.5))
res_s3m <- run_grid(grid_s3m, one_s3m, "make_s3m")
res_s3m$pairs <- res_s3m$sets * 12
write.csv(res_s3m, file.path(OUT, "power_study3_matched.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
kable(res_s3m[order(res_s3m$share, res_s3m$delta, res_s3m$pairs, res_s3m$n), c("share", "delta", "pairs", "n", "type_sig", "se")], digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
      caption = "Study 3, matched sets: power by the share of pair variance common to a matched set")
```

# Study 4: two works, their arrangement, and the side one is on

**Design simulated.** Each participant judges eight pairs of synopses, one in each combination of the kind of shared features (high or low prevalence crossed with high or low distinctiveness) and arrangement (aligned or scattered). Each pair of synopses is built on a story shell; a participant sees eight different shells, and across participants every shell appears in every combination. Role (plaintiff's side, defendant's side, neutral) varies between participants. The judgment is the probability of copying, 0 to 100.

**Assumed values (not from data).** Participant SD 14 points; participant slope for arrangement SD 8; shell SD 6; a separate deviation for each shell-by-condition version, SD 5; residual SD 18. Effects: arrangement +12; low against high prevalence of the shared features +8; distinctiveness either 0 or −8; plaintiff's side +6 and defendant's side −6 against neutral; arrangement by prevalence interaction +6 or +9.

```{r sim-study4}
make_s4 <- function(n_role, shells, bD, bAP) {
  n <- 3 * n_role; role <- rep(c(-1, 0, 1), each = n_role)
  cond <- expand.grid(P = c(-.5, .5), D = c(-.5, .5), A = c(-.5, .5))                 # P: +.5 = low prevalence (rarer shared features)
  ver <- expand.grid(c = 1:8, shell = seq_len(shells)); ver$v <- rnorm(nrow(ver), 0, 5); sh <- rnorm(shells, 0, 6)
  u0 <- rnorm(n, 0, 14); uA <- rnorm(n, 0, 8)
  d <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
    s <- sample(shells, 8); x <- cbind(cond, c = 1:8, shell = s, pid = i, role = role[i]); x }))
  d$version <- (d$shell - 1) * 8 + d$c
  d$y <- 50 + (12 + uA[d$pid]) * d$A + 8 * d$P + bD * d$D + bAP * d$A * d$P + 6 * d$role + u0[d$pid] + sh[d$shell] + ver$v[d$version] + rnorm(nrow(d), 0, 18)
  d
}
one_s4 <- function(g, s) {
  d <- make_s4(g$n_role, g$shells, g$bD, g$bAP)
  m <- lmer(y ~ A * P + A * D + role + (1 | pid) + (0 + A | pid) + (1 | shell) + (1 | version), d, control = CTRL)
  z <- function(L) as.numeric(abs(wald(m, L)["z"]) > 1.96)
  c(arrangement = z(c(A = 1)), prevalence = z(c(P = 1)), distinctiveness = z(c(D = 1)), role = z(c(role = 1)), arrangement_by_prevalence = z(c("A:P" = 1)),
    se_D = as.numeric(wald(m, c(D = 1))["se"]))
}
grid_s4 <- expand.grid(n_role = c(50, 70, 90), shells = c(12, 18), bD = c(0, -8), bAP = c(6, 9))
res_s4 <- run_grid(grid_s4, one_s4, "make_s4")
write.csv(res_s4, file.path(OUT, "power_study4.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
kable(res_s4[order(res_s4$bAP, res_s4$bD, res_s4$shells, res_s4$n_role), ], digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
      caption = "Study 4: power for each effect (n_role = participants per role; the distinctiveness column is the false-positive rate when bD is 0)")
```

# Study 5: showing the counts

**Design simulated.** Participants are told the counts for each claimed similarity in one of several formats (the format varies between participants) and rate whether each feature is stock. The test is the difference between the prevalence-only and distinctiveness-only formats in the gap between features that are characteristic but rare (LH) and features that are common but not characteristic (HL). Study 1 puts that gap at about 0.8 rating points with no counts shown. The simulation asks how large a shift between the two formats can be detected; a full reversal would be a shift of two points or more. Each participant rates 24 features (two per cell in each of three genres) drawn from 48. Item and participant SDs are Study 1's; each item has a separate deviation in each format, SD 0.5 (assumed).

```{r sim-study5}
make_s5 <- function(n_arm, shift) {
  items <- expand.grid(k = 1:2, cell = c("HH", "HL", "LH", "LL"), genre = 1:6, stringsAsFactors = FALSE); items$item <- seq_len(nrow(items))
  w <- rnorm(nrow(items), 0, S1$item); wa <- matrix(rnorm(nrow(items) * 2, 0, 0.5), ncol = 2)
  n <- 2 * n_arm; arm <- rep(c(-.5, .5), each = n_arm); u0 <- rnorm(n, 0, S1$pid)
  d <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) { x <- items[items$genre %in% sample(6, 3), ]; x$pid <- i; x$arm <- arm[i]; x }))
  d <- d[d$cell %in% c("HL", "LH"), ]; d$lh <- ifelse(d$cell == "LH", .5, -.5)
  d$y <- 4.5 + (0.8 + shift * d$arm) * d$lh + u0[d$pid] + w[d$item] + wa[cbind(d$item, ifelse(d$arm > 0, 2, 1))] + rnorm(nrow(d), 0, S1$resid)
  d
}
one_s5 <- function(g, s) {
  d <- make_s5(g$n_arm, g$shift)
  m <- lmer(y ~ lh * arm + (1 | pid) + (1 | item), d, control = CTRL)
  w <- wald(m, c("lh:arm" = 1)); c(format_by_cell = as.numeric(abs(w["z"]) > 1.96), se = as.numeric(w["se"]))
}
grid_s5 <- expand.grid(n_arm = c(40, 60, 80), shift = c(0.6, 0.8, 1.0))
res_s5 <- run_grid(grid_s5, one_s5, "make_s5")
write.csv(res_s5, file.path(OUT, "power_study5.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
kable(res_s5[order(res_s5$shift, res_s5$n_arm), ], digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
      caption = "Study 5: power to detect a shift (in rating points) between two count formats in the LH-minus-HL gap (n_arm = participants per format)")
```
